protocol.runtime: spawned by HCLI's own RuntimePool, not an attached server
protocol.ordering: alternating paired reps, interleaved rather than blocked, so page-cache and thermal drift is common-mode
protocol.equilibrium_rule: the highest rung whose median aggregate tok/s beats its predecessor by more than the observed measurement spread
protocol.machine_state: quiet: zero grok-run lanes in flight for every run below

finding.detail: On the 5-slot pool the ladder reads 22.489 / 24.839 / 26.050 / 28.422 / 28.259 tok/s aggregate for c=1..5, i.e. 1.000 / 1.105 / 1.159 / 1.264 / 1.257. Aggregate peaks at FOUR concurrent decodes and goes DOWN at five. Concurrency is a real but small lever here: four decoders buy 26% over one, not 4x.

slot_count_costs_single_stream_throughpu.note: A pool allocated for five sequences decodes a SINGLE stream about 5% slower than one allocated for two. Scaling ratios are therefore only compared within a run, never across runs, because each run's own c=1 is its baseline.

reproducibility.note: Two independent runs agree to under 0.3%, and the tightest single rung spread is 0.03%. Compare the first attempt at this measurement, which was taken with ten grok lanes in flight and showed a 50% spread; it was recorded as CONTAMINATED and rejected rather than reported.

contradicts_the_machine_genome.note: ~/.config/hcli/machine_genome.json understates the limit (2 vs a measured 4) and overstates what two decoders buy (1.1934 claimed vs 1.105 measured). The genome was not edited: it is the operator's qualified profile, and changing it is a separate decision.
